summary: A for loop repeats commands once for each item in a list. A while loop repeats as long as a test is true, and while read goes through a file line by line.
notes: for file in cs/*.java runs once with the text cs/*.java, because no file matched. Check with [ -e "$file" ] if that can happen.
done < cs/grades.csv feeds the file into the whole while loop, so read gets the next line each time around.
$((honor + 1)) does whole-number math. The loop body runs between do and done.
pitfall: Piping into a while loop (cat cs/grades.csv | while read ...) runs the loop in a separate shell, so honor is still 0 after done. Use done < cs/grades.csv instead.
